chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ahmad and Muhammad, the sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Hasan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about jewelry (al-huliy), is there zakat in it? He said, 'Indeed, there is no zakat in it, even if it reaches one hundred thousand dirhams, and my father differs with the people in this.' As for that which indicates that whenever he is exempted from it, the zakat becomes obligatory upon him, is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is there zakat on jewelry in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia jurisprudential stance that gold jewelry intended for personal use is exempt from zakat, even if its value exceeds the nisab threshold of one hundred thousand dirhams. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly contrasts this ruling with the prevailing opinion of 'the people' (often interpreted as the general public or other schools of thought), emphasizing a distinction between wealth held for utility versus wealth held for accumulation. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that zakat applies primarily to stored wealth and trade goods, rather than items consumed in daily life.
